name: Egusi Soup
summary: A rich, nutty soup of ground melon seeds simmered in palm oil with leaves, crayfish and assorted meats.
story: Egusi, made from the ground seeds of a type of melon, is one of the most widely cooked soups in Nigeria, found in many regions with small variations. It is typically eaten with a swallow such as pounded yam or eba at family meals and gatherings. Some cooks like it in loose curds, others smooth and thick.

items.name: Scotch bonnet and red bell pepper

steps.title: Cook the meat
steps.text: Season the meat with onion, stock cubes and salt, add a splash of water and cook covered until tender, about 40 minutes for beef. Add the soaked stockfish for the last 15 minutes, and keep the stock.

steps.title: Heat the palm oil
steps.text: In a wide pot warm the palm oil over medium heat for 2 minutes, just until it is hot and slightly shimmering. Do not let it smoke.

steps.title: Fry the pepper blend
steps.text: Add the blended peppers and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the water has gone and the sauce has darkened and thickened.

steps.title: Make egusi paste
steps.text: Mix the ground egusi with a few spoonfuls of water to form a thick paste. Spoon it into the pot in clumps and leave undisturbed for 5 minutes so the underside sets.

steps.title: Fry the curds
steps.text: Stir gently and fry for 8 to 10 minutes, until the egusi forms soft curds, looks golden and releases a nutty smell. Add the crayfish and iru.

steps.title: Add stock and meat
steps.text: Pour in about 2 cups of the meat stock, add the meat and stockfish, and simmer on low for 15 minutes. The oil should rise to the top; add a little stock if it gets too thick.

steps.title: Add the leaves
steps.text: Stir in the chopped leaves and cook for 3 to 5 minutes only, so they stay green and slightly firm. Taste and adjust salt before serving.

tips: Do not add all the water at once; egusi should fry before it boils, which is what makes the curds.
Keep the heat moderate when frying egusi because the seeds scorch quickly.
Add leaves last and briefly to keep their colour.

swaps.swap: Ground pumpkin seeds (pepitas) are the closest substitute; the soup will taste slightly greener and less rich.
Use spinach, kale or collard greens; the soup will be milder and not bitter.
Use extra crayfish or a spoon of fish sauce for savoury depth.
